utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Mr. Praljak is planning to have his own questions. It is mostly about electricity. As you have heard, this witness is electrical engineer, the same diploma as Mr. Praljak, and this is good opportunity as many of those issues are raised on the direct examination but some areas are not covered. And perhaps Mr. Praljak will have additional, couple of questions, to that main subject. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, in other words, Mr. Praljak is also an -- or was an electrical engineer or still is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's what I said. Perhaps it was lost in translation, but we know that from his CV. It's stated in his indictment and we never challenged this claim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I just may add a point. You have stated, Mr. Kovacic, that he would cover lacuna in direct. So are we to understand that he is in a way continuing direct rather than cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. He will follow-up on the topics that were raised, but you will see that we will go through some documents. But in essence, this is the cross-examination because some topics were raised but there are other questions to pursue on those topics, so it qualifies as cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last question, Mr. Kovacic. How much time do you need roughly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our estimate that Mr. Praljak could need about one hour, bearing in mind the length of the examination-in-chief and the time that the Defence -- other Defence teams are given, no other teams have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So if there were other Defence teams they would only have 30 minutes. Mr. Praljak, we have ten minutes left today. Let's go ahead. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to note that this is a good opportunity for a top electrical engineer, Mr. Kozulj, to testify here so that we could finish with electricity and the telephone connections and those problems because it seemed to me that this problem was being simplified technically and that it seemed as if all of that could be done at home or a do-it-yourself kind of thing in 24 hours. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anyway, good evening, Mr. Kozulj.

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we don't have that much time, I'm going to change my order. I wanted to start with something else, but I will change that. Look at 1D 00549, 1D 00549. It's a document that has just been distributed to Their Honours and to you. It's a document of the 29th of May, 1992. We're going to look at this first item which says: "For the purpose of" -- oh, "in order to prevent unauthorised connection or disconnection of electricity supply for consumers, guard or secure all 10/0.4 kilowatt transformer stations in local communes." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall the document setting out the priorities to repair the electrical supply network?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So can you please tell me, where does this conclusion come from that you can just arbitrarily switch on or off these transformer stations? Do we agree that there are people who take a key, they open up the transformer station, and switch their area on if they want; so in order to prevent this from happening, they needed to be or these transformer stations needed to be placed under guard?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: At that time there were power cuts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to recall a rule that has been recalled many times, mostly once when we had a witness from -- who speaks B/C/S. When you have been presented by a question, it first must be translated into English so that we understand it. If you answer immediately much gets lost. So if you could perhaps start again with your answer. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I apologise. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: According to you, did this cover the possibility for somebody to arbitrarily switch electricity on or off, regardless of any instructions, and was it therefore needed to guard the transformer stations?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: I think -- I don't know of any cases, of anyone doing anything arbitrarily, but that possibility always existed. So if there were limitations to the use of electricity and there was an attempt to secure supply only for priority consumers, then it's possible that in such a situation somebody behaved badly and tried to get access to the transformer station without authorisation and reconnect. So in order to prevent anything like that from happening, the mayor of Mostar asked that special attention be paid for that -- to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So we're going to look at this document of the 10th of April in order to look at power-plants, regarding -- regardless of whether they're hydro, nuclear, or thermal power-plants, what would be the voltage of electricity use?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: It would be high-voltage electricity that's being used. The power-plants produced -- to tell you the truth, high-frequency or high-voltage electricity, and it's manufactured in that form because it is being transmitted via the power-supply network.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Praljak, you have just spoken and referred to this document of the 10th of April. Now, the one we have here is 29th of May, and I wonder whether it was a slip of a tongue or whether you had another document in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I did not make a mistake. I think there was a mistake in the translation -- did I make a mistake? No, no, it was a mistake in the translation. Whatever it was, I said it correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I was not blaming you or something, but I wanted to avoid that there is something strange in the transcript. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, of course you are there to warn me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Witness, can you clarify why does electricity have to be a high-voltage one in order to transmit it? Why does electricity have to be raised to 10 kilovolts, 35 kilovolts or 110 or 230 kilovolts to 430 kilovolts? Why is this necessary?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Because -- well, it's a technical question but I'm going to try to explain it in the simplest possible way. If you have consumption of electricity, specific consumption, then the electricity that goes through the distribution network is connected to the voltage. If you have a certain voltage, the electricity would be its power divided by its voltage. So you have the power divided by the voltage. The higher the voltage, the less electricity in the line, so less is lost in the transmission and the frequency doesn't fall. If the distance at which the electricity needs to be transmitted, the voltage at which it is transmitted is higher. I think that is the simplest way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Mr. Engineer or Mr. Minister, I don't know what title to give you, you've just said something, but isn't there a mathematical formula which would be that P = VI square or power is a voltage multiplied by intensity to the square --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] O times E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So can we agree the strength times the voltage would equal the strength of the electricity. If the voltage is higher, the electricity proportionally needs to be lower in order to transmit the same amount and the electricity has to be lower because electricity that passes through the lines warms or heats up the lines and a lot of that energy is just lost in the air; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Yes, losses are increased, and if you would like more not only is the energy lost while it is being transmitted but also the voltage at the end of the consumer is less. So instead of the consumer receiving 220 volts, he receives only 150 volts, which is actually not good for that consumer because they cannot operate their machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. You said that the transformer station and the switching stations, Cule, received voltage of 400 kilovolts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now this is my question: If 400 kilovolts, 4.000 [as interpreted] volts, needs to be reduced to 220 volts, is this possible to do with only one transformer station?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Again, I'm trying to assist you, there may be -- I'm sorry, there may be a loss in translation. 400 kilovolts, are they not 400.000 rather than 4.000 volts? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a mistake in the translation. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I think I said it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you explain to our honourable auditorium why this is not possible to do in one transformer station. We're not going to go into all the types of current and so on and so forth, Tesla's theorys, but if you can just please tell us why essentially this is not possible.

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Well, there are many reasons why this is not possible, but also in practice this is never essential. You never have one consumer or one group of consumers. Usually such large transformer stations have two or three power transmission lines of the highest possible voltage, 400 kilovolts. You also have a large number of smaller transmission lines of 220, 110, and even 35 kilovolts. So that means that you need to transform that first from 400 to 220 and then from 220 to 110 and then 110 to 35, and then we also need to transfer it from 35 to 10 or 20 at the consumer's end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or as we see in this document, to 0.4 kilovolts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ
utterances.text: Yes, from 35, so from the transformer station, the large one, the transmission line goes at least to 35, that's the lowest, and there it's transformed to 10 or 20 kilovolts and then continues to be transformed in some settlement or some small company from 10 or 20 to 0.4 and this is the electricity that is being consumed in the households.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for those who have failed to understand, they have the whole night to think it over. We shall continue tomorrow. We shall be starting at 2.15. Have a very good evening. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 25
